company.name: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence

profile_text.body:
The Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence, also known as Stanford HAI, is a non-profit university lab founded in 2019 and headquartered in Stanford, CA, USA. It describes its mission as advancing humanity through AI and data science, with work focused on discovery, technological innovation, educational transformation, and societal impact. The institute says it studies, guides, and develops human-centered AI technologies and applications, and that AI should be collaborative, augmentative, and enhancing human productivity and quality of life. It is led by Denning Director James Landay, a computer scientist; co-founder Fei-Fei Li serves as Special Advisor on AI and joins John Hennessy as co-chair of the institute's advisory council.

The site does not list commercial AI products. It describes educational programs for leaders, policymakers, civil servants, K-12 educators, and students, along with fellowship and grant programs for interdisciplinary AI research. Its policy work includes evidence-based research and global convenings on AI governance. The site also presents commentary from policy fellows such as Riana Pfefferkorn and Jennifer King, and research from Stanford Law School on local statutes, as well as work on AI in healthcare and language digitization. It states that over 6,000 of the world's 7,000-plus living languages remain digitally disadvantaged.

The institute is also known as Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI, HAI, and AI Index. No litigation cases are recorded for it, but it has legal exposure in California, with 281 associated matters.
